title: Docker and Amazon ECR
description: Learn Docker fundamentals and push container images to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR).

data.text: Docker packages an application and its dependencies into a container image. Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry) is a fully managed container registry that stores, manages, and deploys Docker images.

A Docker container is a lightweight, standalone package that includes everything needed to run a piece of software: code, runtime, libraries, and configuration. Containers are isolated from each other and from the host system.

data.title: Key Docker Concepts
items: **Image** — a read-only template with instructions for creating a container
**Container** — a runnable instance of an image
**Dockerfile** — a text file that defines how to build an image
**Registry** — a storage and distribution system for Docker images

data.text: Amazon ECR is a managed container registry. It integrates with ECS, EKS, and Lambda. You push images to ECR once and pull them from anywhere. ECR supports image scanning for vulnerabilities and lifecycle policies to clean up old images.

Image lifecycle policies automatically expire images based on rules you define. Image scanning checks for known vulnerabilities in your container images using the CVE database. ECR also supports cross-Region replication for disaster recovery.

data.title: Dockerfile Example
data.content: A simple Dockerfile for a Python web application.
data.code:
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "app:app"]

data.title: Build, Tag, and Push to ECR with AWS CLI
data.content: Authenticate Docker to ECR, build an image, and push it to your repository.
data.code:
# Authenticate Docker to ECR
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | \
  docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

# Build the image
docker build -t my-app .

# Tag the image
docker tag my-app:latest 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-app:latest

# Push to ECR
docker push 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-app:latest

terms.definition: A text file containing instructions to build a Docker image.
A packaged application with its dependencies, ready to run in any Docker-compatible environment.
A collection of related container images in Amazon ECR.
A feature that scans container images for known security vulnerabilities.

data.title: Build and Push Your First Image
data.description: Create a simple Flask app, package it in a Docker image, and push it to Amazon ECR.
steps: Write a simple Flask app (app.py) that returns 'Hello, World!'
Write a Dockerfile that uses python:3.11-slim
Authenticate Docker with ECR using the AWS CLI
Build, tag, and push the image to ECR
data.expectedOutcome: Your Docker image is stored in ECR and ready to be pulled by ECS, EKS, or App Runner.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Docker containers package applications with all dependencies
A Dockerfile defines how to build an image
Amazon ECR stores and manages Docker images securely
ECR integrates with image scanning and lifecycle policies
data.takeaway: ECR is AWS's private Docker registry. Once your image is there, any AWS container service can deploy it.
